main_text.p: aliàs احمق من ابي غبشان Stultior Abu-Gabshano.

p. 43. أجود من حاتم Liberalior Hatemo. Fuit Hatemus من شعرا الجاهلية وكان جوادا يشبه شعره Ille جوده ويصدق قوله فعله Ex Arabum antiquiorum poëtis, & insigni liberalitate vir, cujus carmina ipsius munificentiam referebant, cujusque facta dictorum veritatem obsignabant. Author libri Temthal. Refert idem ipsum mense Rajeb singulis diebus decem Camelos jugulâsse quibus hospites exciperet. Alium autem fuisse ejusdem nominis cujus avaritia in proverbium abierit أخبل من حاتم magis avarus quam Hatemus, De ptiori AlMaidani hæc habet, كان جوادا شجاعا شاعرا منظرا اذا قاتل غلب واذا غنم انهب واذا سيبل وهب واذا ضرب بالقداح فاز واذا سابق سبق واذا اسر اطلق Fuit liberalis, fortis, Poeta, victoriosus, cum pugnaret, vincere cum fortibus contenderet, lucrari, cùm curso certare, anteire, cum captivos cepisset, dimittere.

p. 45. أودى عتيب Periit Atib. Dictérium in eos, qui dum spe salutis inani se lactant, miserè pereunt. Historia à qua originem traxit proverbium, hæc est referentibus AlTauhario, AlMaidanio, & AlFirauzabadio. Tribus istius (Banu Atib scil.) omnes ætatis maturæ viros, cum captivos abduxisset rex quidam, illi se hoc solari solebant أذا كبر صبياننا لم يتركونا حتى يفتكوا ubi ad ætatem pervenerint pueri nostri non definent donec nos liberaverint; ipsi interim omnes

page.notes: The Arabic lines are read from a small, low-resolution scan and are not certain letter by letter: the Arabic of the second paragraph (the poem line beginning شاعرا and the line ending اسر اطلق), the word after "Periit" (أودى عتيب) and the last Arabic line (أذا كبر صبياننا...) may contain errors. The word after "Ille" is also doubtful. The sentence "Dictérium" is printed with an accent in the scan and may be "Dicterium". The Latin spelling "cùm curso" should be checked against "cursu" in the scan. The Arabic line at the foot ends with "omnes" printed beside the signature "Y y". No running head or catchword is visible.
